findings.reason: The protected solution is a direct, concise ragged-grid symmetry scan. Its row, column, word, and character names express genuine matrix concepts, both missing-reflection guards precede access, and no candidate would materially improve it.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 422 and its Python validWordSquare surface. The section-authored Reference preserves the kth-row versus kth-column definition, all three authenticated source examples and explanations, all three constraints, and accessible row/column tables equivalent to the three live source grid images.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064768312. Apart from the required Solution method adapter and List annotation, it is structurally identical to the app-local source: both enumerate every existing cell, reject a missing reflected row or character, compare the reflected character, and return true only after the full scan.

The dense 12-, 30-, and 60-row symmetric grids span 25x in total character count and force inspection of every cell. A fresh exact-source run passes all 13 executions at +0.01 extra growth and a largest 1.01x protected-reference runtime ratio; a correct control that rescans each counterpart row passes every output but fails only the runtime verdict at 42.89x.

The Approach exactly describes reflected-coordinate existence and equality, explains why checking every existing cell also rules out one-sided coordinates, and states O(C) time for total character count C with O(1) auxiliary space.

The authenticated Premium statement was reviewed directly in Chrome. The modular Reference preserves the row-versus-column definition and bound, all three explained source examples, all three constraints, and every row/column fact from the three source grid images through three equivalently complete accessible tables. source_fidelity.json is verified with live-content SHA-256 86e2a21219bca90c59a22d815932b2d752d72fffdc357c06ad07ca97456f0bfc and current hashes for every composed Reference section.

coverage: All three authenticated Premium source examples appear first and in source order with their exact word arrays and lowercase Boolean result literals; each is explicitly tagged as a source example.
The visible maximum ragged square simultaneously covers 500 words and a 500-character first word, while the one-character diagonal case covers both lower bounds.
Dense and ragged valid squares, a character mismatch, a missing reflected row, a missing reflected character, and a mismatch near the final cell exercise every semantic failure mode.

An independent oracle reconstructs each complete row and column string and verified all ten authored results, all three benchmarks, 2,954 exhaustive small arrays, 5,000 randomized arrays, and valid and invalid dense 250,000-character maximum grids.
All ten correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged dense 12-, 30-, and 60-row workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
